record.original_question: If a graph G has maximum degree Delta and contains no cycle of length 5, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= Delta^2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 28 ([144]). If G is a graph with no 5-cycle, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆2.
If G has maximum degree ∆ and has no 5-cycle, then χ_s(G) 6 ∆2. This is Conjecture 28, due to Mahdian.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A strong edge-coloring of a simple graph $G$ is a proper edge-coloring in which every color class is an induced matching; equivalently, any two edges that are joined by an edge or share an endpoint must receive distinct colors. The strong chromatic index $\chi_s(G)$ is the minimum number of colors needed in a strong edge-coloring of $G$. Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$.

Prove or disprove: every simple graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ that contains no cycle of length $5$ satisfies
$$\chi_s(G) \le \Delta^2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is Mahdian's conjecture on the strong chromatic index of C5-free graphs. Mahdian proved an asymptotic bound for C4-free graphs but the Δ² bound for C5-free graphs is listed as an open conjecture in surveys of strong edge-coloring (e.g., West's open problems page). No proof or disproof appears in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Strong Edge-Coloring open problems (West)
status_evidence.snippet: Mahdian conjectured that s'(G) ≤ Δ² when G is C5-free.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is recorded as an open problem on West's open-problems page.

status_evidence.title: The Strong Chromatic Index of C4-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Mahdian proved that for C4-free graphs s'(G) ≤ (2+o(1))Δ²/lnΔ.
status_evidence.claim: Mahdian's work on the C4-free case is the origin of the related C5-free conjecture.
